question.text: What is the penalty under Section 15EA for default by AIFs, InvITs, or REITs?

answer.text: Not less than Rs. 1 lakh, extendable to Rs. 1 lakh per day during the continuing failure, subject to a maximum of Rs. 1 crore or three times the gains made out of the failure, whichever is higher
Minimum Rs. 1 lakh, maximum Rs. 1 crore only
Minimum Rs. 5 lakh, maximum Rs. 25 crore
Minimum Rs. 10 lakh, maximum Rs. 50 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 15EA applies to AIFs, InvITs, and REITs for failure to comply with SEBI regulations or directions. The penalty is not less than Rs. 1 lakh, may extend to Rs. 1 lakh for each day during which the failure continues, and is capped at Rs. 1 crore or three times the gains made out of the failure, whichever is higher. The Trap: Rs. 1 lakh is the statutory minimum, not the minimum per-day amount. The per-day figure is the extension rate, and the cap uses the higher of Rs. 1 crore or three times gains. Note: The "three times gains" alternative cap is the feature that distinguishes Section 15EA from default penalty structures that cap only at Rs. 1 crore.
